programme: IRF3 and ATF2 are the two transcription factors that classically assemble (together with NF-κB, not in this list) on the IFN-β enhancer to drive type I interferon transcription — the 'IFN-β enhanceosome'; STAT5A sits downstream as the JAK-STAT relay that converts cytokine/interferon receptor engagement into a T-cell/immune transcriptional programme. Together IRF3+ATF2+STAT5A describe a coherent innate-interferon-to-JAK/STAT signaling axis, not three independent hits.
role_in_a: In multiple sclerosis, IRF3 is activated through the cGAS/STING-TBK1 sensor pathway in microglia to drive IFN-β production and neuroinflammation (PMID 41265623, PMID 42090738), and STAT5A operates in the downstream cytokine/JAK-STAT loop that shifts with disease-modifying treatment and differs from controls (PMID 39545481, PMID 29126764). ATF2, as the enhanceosome partner that normally co-occupies the IFN-β promoter with IRF3, would be expected to travel with this same microglial interferon response, though no MS-specific paper for ATF2 was retrieved here.
role_in_b: In rectal/colorectal cancer, IRF3-linked interferon signaling shapes tumor immune infiltration and prognosis (PMID 34488791), and interferon-pathway gene variants are associated with colorectal cancer risk (PMID 25350395). STAT5A sits within the JAK/STAT/SOCS axis implicated in colon and rectal cancer (PMID 22121102). ATF2 acts as a brake on invasion: its loss upregulates the driver TROP2 and promotes tumor invasion (PMID 35838828), and an ATF2-linked effector (p57Kip2) functions in the DNA-damage response as a tumor-suppressive mechanism (PMID 25195859).
shared_axis: Both diseases recur through the same generic logic of chronic, dysregulated type-I-interferon/JAK-STAT signaling: in MS this axis is pushed toward sustained microglial IFN-β output and neuroinflammation, while in rectal cancer the same axis shapes tumor-immune crosstalk and, through ATF2, restrains or permits local invasion. The tissues differ, but the enhanceosome-to-JAK/STAT circuitry is not tissue-specific, which is why it can recur independently in a CNS autoimmune disease and a GI epithelial cancer.
reasoning: IRF3 and STAT5A are each independently placed in both diseases by retrieved papers, and one paper (25350395) is explicitly marked as concerning both, so this is not built on silence. But the enhanceosome logic that pulls ATF2 into the story for the MS side rests on established immunology reasoning, not on any retrieved ATF2-MS paper, and rectal-specific (vs. colorectal-general) evidence is thin throughout — so the account is supported rather than established, and moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 41265623 (STING/TBK1/IRF3 activation in microglia in an MS-relevant model); PMID 42090738 (STING-dependent microglial IRF3 axis modulated in experimental autoimmune neuroinflammation); PMID 39545481 (STAT-related gene expression shifts with first-line MS treatment); PMID 29126764 (STAT5a/STAT6 expression altered in MS patients); PMID 34488791 (IRF family, including IRF3, shapes colorectal tumor immunity and prognosis); PMID 25350395 (interferon-signaling-pathway gene SNPs associated with colorectal cancer; record marks it as concerning both diseases); PMID 22121102 (JAK/STAT/SOCS pathway reviewed in colon and rectal cancer); PMID 35838828 (ATF2 loss promotes colorectal invasion via TROP2 upregulation); PMID 25195859 (ATF2-linked p57Kip2 as a DNA-damage-response tumor-suppressor effector).
how_to_falsify: Block STING-TBK1-IRF3 signaling (e.g., STING antagonist or IRF3 knockout/knockdown) in parallel in an MS-relevant microglial/EAE model and in a rectal-cancer tumor-immune model; if silencing IRF3 changes the neuroinflammatory phenotype but has no effect on tumor immune infiltration or invasiveness (or vice versa), the shared-axis claim fails. Separately, ChIP-seq for ATF2 in MS-relevant microglia at IFN-β-responsive loci: if ATF2 does not co-occupy these sites with IRF3 in this cell type, the enhanceosome link assumed for the MS side is wrong.
caveats: Brain vs. colorectal tissue pairing is unusual, and the tissue-generic exclusion list (SOX2, ASCL1, NR3C1, MEF2C, TAL1, ZEB1/2, etc.) already removed the obvious brain/immune master regulators, so this account had to be built from what was left rather than the strongest a priori candidates. Support fractions are modest in absolute terms: even the top factor overall (HHEX, 213/520 = 41%) is concordant in well under half of the 520 patient-group comparisons across 9 cohort pairs, and the three carrying factors here sit at 36-37%. HHEX, despite the highest count, is excluded from this account — its only evidence is an MS GWAS hit, with no rectal-cancer signal anywhere in the record, and it does not fit the interferon/JAK-STAT module. ELF4 is explicitly flagged discordant (unlike the other concordant factors) and is excluded. Most rectal-cancer citations used here are colorectal-cancer literature in general, not rectal-specific; evidence throughout is weighted more toward multiple sclerosis than toward rectal cancer, consistent with the overall record note.
